reuse: All three previously frozen every_step baseline runs, seeds141/142/143, are reused, not selected by performance. Their known arrivals4/10/31 are disclosed. Before new training a full_anchor5000-step run must reproduce the previous seed905 preflight exactly
target_sync_rule: Unchanged reference engine: completed episode end only, after update, replay length>64 and steps since last sync>50
bootstrap: WIN only zero-bootstrap; LOSE continues to bootstrap in every arm

losses.full_anchor: (mean(selected TD squared error)+mean(sum of three unselected Q-policy minus Q-target squared errors))/4

contrasts.full_anchor_vs_selected_quarter: Remove unselected output anchoring at the same selected-error coefficient; optimizer normalization may mediate effects
contrasts.selected_quarter_vs_selected: Multiply the whole selected-only objective by4 at fixed Adam lr; do not interpret this as4x parameter update or equivalent lr change

execution: Use unmodified frozen frequency engine with scoped loss injection and forced every_step schedule. No source edit, feature changes, terminal change, target-sync change, masking, clipping or teacher
random_streams: Same split generators, same initial weights and per-episode reset sequence as the reused reference engine
comparison_scope: All9 models have200000 environment steps and199936 optimizer updates; realized episode count, epsilon and sync timestamps may differ as consequences of trajectories. Same hotel, diagnostic horizon, no paper12000-episode or external validity claim
budget_cut: Retain PLAYING label for final unfinished episode, no fictitious environment terminal or episode-end events
evaluation: Save each fixed-budget final model before all61-start evaluation; no best-checkpoint selection. Both paper paths and all failures retained
stop_rule: Six new finite runs only;900-second per-run hard cap, no automatic retries or adaptive extensions. Reused three baseline runs stay immutable
formula_caveat: Adam approximately cancels constant positive gradient scaling through its moment normalization; epsilon, finite precision and closed-loop trajectory changes may break exact invariance
